title: Uncovering Competing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

problem.claim: Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems are vulnerable to adversaries that seed corpora with manipulated content.

gap.claim: Prior work largely evaluates retrieval poisoning under a simplified single-attacker assumption, despite practical settings involving multiple adversaries with conflicting objectives.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes competing attacks, where multiple attackers simultaneously steer the same or closely related query toward different targets.
The paper proposes competitive effectiveness to quantify an attacker's advantage under competition.
The paper presents PoisonArena, a standardized framework and benchmark for evaluating poisoning attacks and defenses under multi-adversary conditions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that many strategies successful against a single attacker degrade markedly under competition.
The authors report performance inversions and limitations of attack success rate and F1 under competition.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG improves factual grounding but remains vulnerable to retrieval poisoning.
Existing evaluations largely assume one attacker, while high-value queries may attract multiple adversaries with conflicting objectives.
The paper introduces competing attacks and formalizes the threat model with a competitive-effectiveness metric.
Experiments report that single-attacker strategies can degrade under competition and expose performance inversions and metric limitations.
PoisonArena is presented as a standardized benchmark and framework, with project materials and code made available online.

source_observation.claim: Strategies that succeed in a single-attacker regime may degrade markedly when attackers compete.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation results can depend materially on whether adversarial objectives interact.

application.claim: Evaluate retrieval-poisoning attacks and defenses under multi-adversary conditions when competing objectives are plausible.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson generalizes beyond the reported poisoning settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the definition or calculation of competitive effectiveness.
The abstract does not report datasets, attack strategies, defense configurations, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not specify the scope, contents, or evaluation protocol of PoisonArena.
